examples.ko: 창고 문을 열자 고리타분한 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the storeroom door, there was a musty smell.
The old blanket gives off a stale smell.
My father's way of thinking is a bit old-fashioned.
Please stop with that stuffy old talk.
It's damp inside the closet, so it smells stale.

examples.ko: 규칙이 너무 고리타분해서 아무도 안 좋아해요.
examples.en: The rules are so outdated and stuffy that nobody likes them.

explain: 냄새가 퀴퀴할 때도 쓰지만, 생각이나 방식이 낡고 답답할 때 더 많이 써요. '구식이다'나 '케케묵다'와 비슷해요. 상대방에게 직접 말하면 무례하게 들려요.
explain_en: It can describe a stale smell, but it is more often used for thinking or methods that feel outdated and stuffy. It is close to '구식이다' and '케케묵다'. Saying it directly to someone sounds rude.

examples.en: My grandfather is really stubborn.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 고집불통이라서 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: He's so hardheaded that you can't reason with him.
It's not easy to persuade my stubborn younger sibling.

examples.ko: 남편이 고집불통이라 매번 제가 져 줘요.
examples.en: My husband is so stubborn that I always give in.
Working under a stubborn boss is hard.
If you act so stubborn, you'll lose your friends.

explain: 사람을 흉볼 때 쓰는 말이라서 대부분 좋지 않은 느낌이에요. '고집쟁이'보다 훨씬 세서 아예 말이 안 통한다는 느낌이 있어요. '고집이 세다'는 조금 더 부드러운 표현이에요.
explain_en: This is used to criticize a person, so it usually sounds negative. It is much stronger than '고집쟁이', suggesting someone you simply can't reason with. '고집이 세다' is a softer way to say it.

examples.en: My father's cell phone is totally outdated.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 생각이 구닥다리라서 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: His thinking is so old-fashioned that we can't communicate.
It's an ancient computer, so the programs are very slow.
I was a bit upset to be treated as old-fashioned.

examples.ko: 구닥다리인 줄 알았는데 써 보니 쓸 만해요.
examples.en: I thought it was outdated, but it turns out to be quite usable.
Please don't see me as old-fashioned.

explain: 물건, 생각, 사람에게 다 쓸 수 있어요. 중립적인 '구식'보다 낮추는 느낌이 강해서, 친한 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰거나 윗사람에게는 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It can be used for objects, ideas and people. It sounds more belittling than the neutral '구식', so it fits jokes among close friends, and you should be careful using it about someone older.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 성격 차이가 극명히 드러났어요.
examples.en: The difference in the two people's personalities became strikingly clear.

examples.ko: 이 사진이 그날의 상황을 극명히 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo shows the situation that day very clearly.
The results were so starkly different that everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 이 실험은 그 차이를 극명히 증명했어요.
examples.en: This experiment proved that difference unmistakably.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 생활 모습이 극명히 대비돼요.
examples.en: The way of life in the two countries contrasts sharply.

examples.ko: 점수가 극명히 갈린 걸 보면 준비 차이가 컸어요.
examples.en: Seeing how sharply the scores split, the difference in preparation was big.

explain: 차이나 모습이 아주 뚜렷하게 보일 때 써요. 주로 '드러나다', '보여 주다', '대비되다', '갈리다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 말할 때는 '극명하게'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a difference or appearance is very clear. It mostly appears with words like '드러나다' (be revealed), '보여 주다' (show), '대비되다' (contrast) and '갈리다' (split). In speech people also say '극명하게'.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 근대식으로 지어져서 분위기가 독특해요.
examples.en: This building was built in a modern-era style, so it has a unique atmosphere.
My grandfather is from the generation that received modern-style education.

examples.ko: 근대식 병원이 처음 생긴 때를 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned when the first modern-style hospital appeared.

examples.ko: 거리에 근대식 건물이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Some modern-era buildings still remain on the street.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 근대식 교실을 그대로 보존했어요.
examples.en: That school preserved its modern-era classroom as it was.

examples.ko: 근대식 설비를 들여와 공장을 새로 지었어요.
examples.en: They brought in modern equipment and built the factory anew.

explain: '전통식'과 반대로, 개화기 이후 서양에서 들어온 방식이나 모양을 말해요. 보통 '근대식 건물', '근대식 교육'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. '현대식'은 지금 쓰는 최신 방식이라 시기가 달라요.
explain_en: In contrast to '전통식' (traditional style), it refers to methods or looks that came from the West after the opening of the country. It is usually placed before a noun, as in '근대식 건물' and '근대식 교육'. '현대식' means today's up-to-date style, so the era is different.

examples.en: My hands are so rough.
I haven't slept for days, so my skin is rough and dull.
I wiped my face with a scratchy towel.
I didn't shave, so my chin got stubbly.
In winter my lips get rough, so I put on balm.
The surface of this paper is rough.

explain: '꺼칠하다'를 반복해서 거칠고 마른 느낌을 더 강조한 말이에요. 피부, 입술, 머리카락, 수염처럼 만졌을 때 매끄럽지 않은 것에 많이 써요. 반대로 매끄럽고 부드러우면 '부드럽다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It repeats '꺼칠하다' to stress a rough, dry feel. It is common for skin, lips, hair and stubble, things that feel not smooth to the touch. The opposite is '부드럽다' (soft, smooth).

examples.ko: 선생님은 늘 나긋나긋한 목소리로 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: The teacher always explains in a soft, gentle voice.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 나긋나긋해서 듣기 편해요.
examples.en: That person's way of speaking is gentle, so it's easy to listen to.

examples.ko: 화가 났는데도 나긋나긋하게 말해서 더 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Even though she was angry, she spoke so softly that it was even scarier.

examples.ko: 나긋나긋하지만 할 말은 다 하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: She is gentle but says everything she needs to say.

examples.ko: 처음 만났을 때 그 사람은 아주 나긋나긋했어요.
examples.en: When we first met, that person was very gentle.
Just because someone is soft-spoken doesn't mean they are weak.

explain: 주로 말투, 목소리, 태도가 부드럽고 상냥할 때 써요. 반대로 무뚝뚝하고 거칠게 말하는 모습에는 '퉁명스럽다'를 써요. 칭찬으로 쓰이는 일이 많지만, 겉으로만 부드러운 사람을 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when someone's way of speaking, voice or attitude is soft and kind. The opposite, curt and rough speech, is '퉁명스럽다'. It is often a compliment, but it can also describe someone who is only gentle on the surface.

examples.ko: 저는 내향성이 강해서 사람 많은 곳이 피곤해요.
examples.en: I'm quite introverted, so crowded places tire me out.

examples.ko: 내향성인 사람도 발표를 잘할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Introverted people can give good presentations too.

examples.ko: 내향성과 외향성 중에서 나는 어디에 가까울까요?
examples.en: Between introversion and extroversion, which am I closer to?

examples.ko: 친구는 내향성 성격이라 조용한 카페를 좋아해요.
examples.en: My friend has an introverted personality, so she likes quiet cafés.
Introversion is not a flaw but just one type of personality.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 내향성 때문에 낯선 모임을 힘들어해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling finds unfamiliar gatherings hard because of introversion.

explain: 반대말은 '외향성'이에요. 사람을 직접 말할 때는 '내향적이다', '내향적인 사람'이 더 자연스럽고, '내향성'은 성격 특성을 설명할 때 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '외향성' (extroversion). When describing a person directly, '내향적이다' or '내향적인 사람' sounds more natural, while '내향성' is used to talk about the trait itself.

examples.en: The bread has baked to a light golden yellow.
Now that it's autumn, the ginkgo leaves are turning yellowish.
The yellowish curry looks delicious.
Fry the egg until it turns a light golden color.
The wallpaper turned yellowish in the sunlight.
I spread soft, pale yellow butter on the bread.

explain: '노랗다'보다 색이 옅고 부드러운 노란빛을 말해요. 빵이나 전처럼 구워진 것, 낙엽이나 종이처럼 색이 변한 것에 잘 어울려요. 구워진 모습은 '노릇노릇'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a paler, softer yellow than '노랗다'. It suits things that are baked, such as bread or jeon, and things whose color has changed, like fallen leaves or paper. The look of well-baked food can also be called '노릇노릇'.

examples.en: The old paper has turned a dingy yellow.

examples.ko: 형광등 불빛 아래라서 얼굴이 누리끼리해 보여요.
examples.en: Under the fluorescent light, your face looks sallow.
The white shirt has turned yellowish after wearing it for so long.
I want to make my yellowed teeth white.
The wallpaper has yellowed, so we decided to replace it.

examples.ko: 오래된 책은 종이가 누리끼리하고 냄새도 나요.
examples.en: Old books have yellowed pages and a musty smell.

explain: '노랗다'가 산뜻한 노란색이라면 이 말은 탁하고 칙칙한 누런색이에요. 오래된 종이, 낡은 옷, 안 좋은 안색처럼 별로 좋지 않은 느낌으로 써요. '누렇다', '누르스름하다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: While '노랗다' is a bright, clean yellow, this word is a dull, murky yellow. It is used with a negative feel, for old paper, worn clothes or an unhealthy complexion. It is similar to '누렇다' and '누르스름하다'.

examples.en: Everyone was surprised by that child's boldness.
This job needs a little boldness.

examples.ko: 신인 감독의 대담성이 영화 곳곳에서 느껴져요.
examples.en: The new director's boldness can be felt throughout the film.
He has boldness, but he is quite unprepared.
The interviewers thought highly of his boldness.

examples.ko: 그는 대담성과 신중함을 모두 갖춘 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is a person who has both boldness and caution.

explain: '대담하다'의 성질을 말할 때 쓰고 '대담성이 있다/없다/부족하다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '배짱', '용기'가 있고 반대되는 말은 '소심함'이에요. 칭찬할 때도 쓰지만 '무모함'에 가까운 뜻으로 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It names the quality of being '대담하다' (bold), as in '대담성이 있다/없다/부족하다'. Close words are '배짱' and '용기', and the opposite is '소심함'. It can be praise, but sometimes it leans toward recklessness.

examples.ko: 지금 두 나라는 서로 대립적 관계에 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries are now in an opposing relationship.

examples.ko: 대립적 입장을 가진 사람들이 오늘 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: People with opposing positions met for the first time today.

examples.ko: 이 둘을 대립적 개념으로만 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't see these two only as opposing concepts.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 선과 악의 대립적 구도로 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: The film is built on an opposing structure of good and evil.

examples.ko: 지금은 대립적 상황이라서 결론이 안 나요.
examples.en: It is a situation of opposition right now, so no conclusion is reached.

examples.ko: 무조건 대립적 시각으로만 보지 말고 함께 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think together instead of always seeing it from an opposing view.

explain: '대립적 관계', '대립적 입장'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 서술할 때는 '대립적이다'나 '대립적인'으로 말하기도 해요. 서로 맞서거나 반대되는 상태를 말하는 글이나 토론에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '대립적 관계' or '대립적 입장'. You can also say '대립적이다' or '대립적인'. It appears often in writing and debates about things that oppose or contrast each other.

examples.en: The two people's personalities contrast with each other.

examples.ko: 밝은 색과 어두운 색이 크게 대비되는 그림이에요.
examples.en: It's a painting where bright and dark colors contrast strongly.
The result was a contrast with last year's.

examples.ko: 하얀 옷이 검은 배경과 잘 대비돼서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The white clothes contrast well with the black background, so they stand out.
The older and younger brothers contrasted, starting from their height.

examples.ko: 좋은 점과 나쁜 점이 대비되게 정리했어요.
examples.en: I organized the good and bad points so they contrast.

explain: 두 가지를 나란히 놓았을 때 차이가 뚜렷하게 보인다는 뜻이에요. '비교되다'는 어느 쪽이 나은지 견주는 느낌이 있고, '대비되다'는 차이가 서로 반대처럼 선명한 느낌이에요. '대비하다'는 '준비하다'라는 전혀 다른 뜻이니 구분하세요.
explain_en: It means a difference stands out clearly when two things are set side by side. 비교되다 leans toward judging which is better, while 대비되다 stresses a sharp, almost opposite difference. Be careful: 대비하다 is a different word meaning to prepare for something.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 시내에서 멀리 동떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: This village is far removed from downtown.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 생각은 현실과 너무 동떨어졌어요.
examples.en: His thinking is too far from reality.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 큰길에서 동떨어진 곳에 있어요.
examples.en: Our house is in a place remote from the main road.
If what you say is out of touch with the situation, it's hard to understand.

examples.ko: 그 의견은 사실과 동떨어져서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: That opinion is far from the facts, so it's hard to believe.

examples.ko: 가끔은 세상과 동떨어져 살고 싶을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I want to live cut off from the world.

explain: 장소가 멀리 떨어져 있을 때뿐 아니라 생각이나 말이 현실과 맞지 않을 때도 써요. 'A와/에서 동떨어지다' 형태로 쓰고, '동떨어진 곳/이야기'처럼 -ㄴ 형태로 뒤에 명사를 꾸미는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is used both for places that are far away and for ideas or words that don't match reality. It takes the pattern 'A와/에서 동떨어지다', and the '-ㄴ' form is common before a noun, as in '동떨어진 곳/이야기'.

examples.en: There are many round, smooth stones by the river.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 성격이 둥글둥글해서 친구가 많아요.
examples.en: He has an easygoing personality, so he has many friends.
Please shape the dough into round balls.
The baby is round and cute-looking.
I made the snowman nice and round.

examples.ko: 할머니는 둥글둥글 큰 호박을 따 오셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma brought a big, round pumpkin she had picked.

explain: 모양이 모나지 않고 둥근 것뿐 아니라, 성격이 부드럽고 원만하다는 칭찬으로도 써요. 성격 이야기에서는 '둥글둥글하다'로 많이 말하고, 반대는 '모나다'예요.
explain_en: Besides round shapes without corners, it is also a compliment for a gentle, easygoing personality. For personality it is usually said as '둥글둥글하다', and the opposite is '모나다'.

examples.en: It's the summer holiday season, so the beach is teeming with people.
That old warehouse was swarming with rats.

examples.ko: 벌레가 득실거리는 곳에서는 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep in a place crawling with bugs.

examples.ko: 주말 시장에는 관광객이 득실거리고 정말 시끄러워요.
examples.en: The weekend market is packed with tourists and really noisy.
This website is crawling with ads.
During the holidays, every place will be swarming with people.

explain: '장소에 + 사람·벌레·쥐가 + 득실거리다'로 말하고, 많이 모여 어수선하거나 불쾌한 느낌이 있어요. 좋은 느낌 없이 가볍게 '많다'고 할 때는 '바글바글하다'가 더 일상적이에요.
explain_en: It follows the pattern 'place + 에 + people/bugs/rats + 이/가 + 득실거리다' and carries a messy or unpleasant feeling about the crowd. For a lighter, more casual 'crowded', '바글바글하다' is more common in daily speech.

examples.en: The photo and the real thing are completely different.

examples.ko: 형과 동생은 성격이 딴판이라 자주 부딪혀요.
examples.en: The older and younger brothers have totally different personalities, so they often clash.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 만난 친구가 예전과 딴판이어서 못 알아봤어요.
examples.en: My friend, whom I met after a long time, was so different from before that I didn't recognize him.

examples.ko: 말과 행동이 딴판인 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to trust someone whose words and actions are completely different.
This exam was easy, nothing like the last one.
The atmosphere was totally different from what I had expected.

explain: 보통 '~와/과 딴판이다'로 써서 '완전히 다르다'는 강한 느낌을 줘요. 그냥 '다르다'보다 놀라움이나 실망이 담길 때가 많아요. 딱딱한 말로는 '판이하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '~와/과 딴판이다' and sounds stronger than a plain '다르다'. It often carries surprise or disappointment. A stiffer, more formal word with a similar meaning is '판이하다'.

examples.en: That person is incredibly, brutishly strong.
A tremendous downpour came and the roads were blocked.
I was shocked to see my friend eat so ferociously.

examples.ko: 선생님이 숙제를 무지막지하게 많이 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave us an insanely large amount of homework.
The price was outrageous, so I just left.
I carried a ridiculously heavy load by myself.

explain: 원래는 거칠고 무례하다는 뜻인데, 요즘은 양이나 힘, 가격이 어이없을 만큼 대단할 때도 많이 써요. 보통 좋은 느낌은 아니고 '너무하다'는 마음이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: Originally it describes someone rough and rude, but today it is also often used when amount, strength or price is shockingly extreme. It usually carries a negative 'that's too much' feeling rather than praise.

examples.en: The eel keeps slipping out of my hands.

examples.ko: 이끼 낀 돌이 미끈미끈 미끄러워서 조심했어요.
examples.en: The mossy stones were slimy and slippery, so I was careful.
After putting on lotion, my skin became silky smooth.

examples.ko: 해초가 발에 미끈미끈 닿는 느낌이 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like the slimy feel of seaweed against my feet.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤라 길이 미끈미끈 미끄러워서 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: The road was slick after the rain, so I walked slowly.

examples.ko: 목욕탕 바닥이 미끈미끈 미끄러우니까 뛰지 마세요.
examples.en: The bathhouse floor is slippery, so don't run.

explain: 뒤에 '미끄럽다', '부드럽다' 같은 말과 함께 쓰거나 '빠져나가다', '닿다' 같은 동작을 꾸며 줘요. 물기나 기름기가 있어서 매끄러운 느낌이에요. '미끌미끌'과 비슷한 느낌으로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used with words like '미끄럽다' (slippery) or '부드럽다' (soft), or to modify actions like '빠져나가다' (slip out) and '닿다' (touch). It conveys a smooth feel caused by moisture or oil. '미끌미끌' is used with a similar feel.

examples.en: I find plain T-shirts the most comfortable.

examples.ko: 민무늬 접시라서 어떤 음식에도 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: It's a plain plate, so it goes well with any food.

examples.ko: 이 커튼은 민무늬라서 방이 깔끔해 보여요.
examples.en: These curtains are plain, so the room looks neat.

examples.ko: 무늬가 있는 것보다 민무늬 양말이 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer plain socks to patterned ones.
I saw plain, undecorated pottery at the museum.
Try hanging a picture on plain wallpaper.

explain: 반대말은 '줄무늬', '꽃무늬'처럼 무늬가 있는 것이에요. '민-'은 '민소매', '민얼굴'처럼 '아무것도 없는'이라는 느낌을 더해요. 옷, 그릇, 벽지를 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is something with a pattern such as '줄무늬' (stripes) or '꽃무늬' (floral). The prefix '민-' adds a sense of 'nothing added', as in '민소매' (sleeveless) and '민얼굴' (bare face). It is often used for clothes, dishes and wallpaper.

examples.en: The complementary color of red is green.

examples.ko: 보색을 쓰면 그림이 더 선명해 보여요.
examples.en: Using complementary colors makes a painting look sharper.
Blue and orange are complementary colors of each other.
The designer added an accent with a complementary color.

examples.ko: 보색끼리 나란히 놓으면 눈에 확 띄어요.
examples.en: Putting complementary colors side by side really catches the eye.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 보색 대비가 강해서 인상적이에요.
examples.en: This outfit has strong complementary contrast, so it's striking.

explain: 색상환에서 서로 맞은편에 있는 색끼리를 말해요. 미술 시간이나 디자인, 옷 코디 이야기에서 나와요. 서로 가까운 색은 '유사색'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to colors that sit opposite each other on the color wheel. It comes up in art class, design and outfit coordination. Colors that sit close together are called '유사색' (analogous colors).

examples.ko: 그 집은 겉만 뻔지르르하지 속은 비었어요.
examples.en: That house looks slick only on the outside, and it's empty inside.
He's all slick talk and no action.
Don't be fooled by flashy packaging.
That shop has a flashy sign and nothing more.
He came out dressed up in flashy clothes.
It looks glossy, but the quality isn't great.

explain: 겉모양은 매끄럽고 번듯한데 속은 별로일 때 부정적으로 써요. '말만 뻔지르르하다', '겉만 뻔지르르하다'처럼 겉과 속이 다르다는 말과 자주 같이 나와요. '번지르르하다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used negatively when something looks smooth and impressive on the outside but is poor inside. It often appears in phrases like '말만 뻔지르르하다' and '겉만 뻔지르르하다', stressing that the outside and inside differ. People also say '번지르르하다'.

examples.en: The picture hanging on the wall is crooked.
He came out wearing his hat at a slant.
The chair is tilted, so it's uncomfortable to sit on.

examples.ko: 그는 요즘 모든 일을 삐딱한 눈으로 봐요.
examples.en: These days he looks at everything with a cynical eye.

examples.ko: 선생님 말에 삐딱하게 대답하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't answer the teacher in a rude, contrary way.
The book is stuck in at an angle.

explain: '삐딱하다'는 물건이 기울어진 모습에도 쓰고, 사람의 마음이나 태도가 곱지 않을 때도 써요. 비슷한 '비뚤다'는 모양이 곧지 않을 때 주로 써요. '삐딱하게'로 가장 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 내 말을 늘 삐딱하게 봐요.
phrases.en: to take something the wrong way
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 기운 것이 아니라 어떤 일을 좋지 않은 쪽으로 해석한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about a tilted gaze; it means reading something in a negative way.

explain_en: '삐딱하다' describes something tilted, and also a person with a sour or contrary attitude. The similar '비뚤다' is used mainly for shapes that are not straight. Most often you hear '삐딱하게'.

examples.ko: 사람의 성숙도는 나이와 꼭 같지 않아요.
examples.en: A person's maturity is not always the same as their age.
Each child's emotional maturity is different.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 작가의 성숙도를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows the author's maturity.
I'm often surprised by my friend's maturity.
The maturity of civic awareness changes society.

examples.ko: 성숙도가 높은 사람은 감정을 잘 조절해요.
examples.en: People with high maturity control their emotions well.

explain: 얼마나 성숙했는지 그 정도를 말하고, '성숙도가 높다/낮다'처럼 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 사회, 작품에도 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '어른스럽다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It expresses the degree of how mature something is, used as '성숙도가 높다/낮다'. It applies to people, societies and works, and in everyday talk '어른스럽다' is often more natural.

examples.en: In the negotiation, we were put in a defensive position.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 수세적 경기를 하다가 한 골을 먹었어요.
examples.en: Our team played defensively and then conceded a goal.

examples.ko: 너무 수세적 태도로는 문제를 풀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't solve the problem with an overly defensive attitude.

examples.ko: 수세적 자세만 지키지 말고 먼저 제안해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just stay on the defensive; try making the first proposal.
The company is switching to a defensive strategy.

examples.ko: 그는 수세적인 말투로 자기 잘못이 아니라고 했어요.
examples.en: He said in a defensive tone that it wasn't his fault.

explain: 반대말은 '공세적'이에요. '수세적 입장', '수세적 태도'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰고, '수세적인', '수세적이다'로도 써요. 협상, 경기, 토론처럼 맞서는 상황에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '공세적' (offensive). It goes before a noun, as in '수세적 입장' or '수세적 태도', and also appears as '수세적인' or '수세적이다'. It is common in confrontational situations such as negotiations, sports and debates.

examples.ko: 악덕 사장 밑에서 일하다가 월급도 못 받았어요.
examples.en: I worked under a ruthless boss and didn't even get paid.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 악덕 업주가 직원들을 괴롭힌 사건이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news reported a case of an unscrupulous owner mistreating employees.

examples.ko: 악덕 임대인이 보증금을 돌려주지 않아서 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: It became a problem because an unscrupulous landlord didn't return the deposit.

examples.ko: 사재기로 값을 올린 악덕 상인을 단속한대요.
examples.en: They say they will crack down on the unscrupulous merchants who raised prices by hoarding.

examples.ko: 그런 악덕 기업은 소비자들이 외면할 거예요.
examples.en: Consumers will turn their backs on an unscrupulous company like that.

examples.ko: 돈에 눈이 멀어 악덕을 일삼는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who, blinded by money, habitually commit wicked acts.

explain: 보통 '악덕 업주', '악덕 기업'처럼 사람이나 회사 앞에 붙여서, 돈을 위해 남을 괴롭히는 나쁜 쪽을 말해요. 반대로 좋은 행동이나 성품은 '미덕'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is usually attached in front of a person or company, as in '악덕 업주' or '악덕 기업', for those who mistreat others for money. The opposite, a good deed or trait, is '미덕' (virtue).

examples.en: The kids came running in, laughing boisterously.
I've never seen such an over-the-top greeting.
It's nothing serious, but you're making too much fuss.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말도 행동도 야단스러워서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: He stands out because both his words and his actions are showy.
Please congratulate her quietly, without a big fuss.
Grandmother greeted her grandchild with a big, fussy delight.

explain: '야단스럽다'는 소리나 행동이 지나치게 크고 요란해서 시끄러운 느낌이 들 때 써요. 비슷한 '호들갑스럽다'는 작은 일을 크게 떠드는 모습에 더 어울려요. 좋은 뜻으로 칭찬할 때는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '야단스럽다' is used when sound or behavior is too big and showy, so it feels noisy. The similar '호들갑스럽다' fits better when someone makes a big deal out of something small. It is rarely a compliment.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 얼굴값을 하는지 연애 소문이 끝이 없어요.
examples.en: That actor seems to live up to his looks, because the dating rumors never end.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼굴값 하느라 연락도 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so full of himself over his looks that he hardly ever contacts me.
If you want to live up to your looks, start by being polite.

examples.ko: 생긴 건 멀쩡한데 얼굴값도 못 하네요.
examples.en: He looks fine, but he doesn't live up to his looks.

examples.ko: 얼굴값 한다는 소리를 들으면 기분이 어때요?
examples.en: How would you feel if people said you were acting like your looks?

examples.ko: 걔는 얼굴값 하는 사람은 아니라서 오히려 편해요.
examples.en: He's not the type to act on his looks, so he's actually easy to be around.

explain: 주로 '얼굴값을 하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 잘생기거나 예쁜 사람이 그 외모에 걸맞게(또는 외모를 믿고) 행동한다는 뜻으로 비꼬는 경우가 많아요. 칭찬으로 쓰기보다는 조금 비꼬는 말투가 되기 쉬워요. 그래서 외모를 칭찬하고 싶을 때는 다른 말을 쓰는 게 안전해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '얼굴값을 하다' and often has a sarcastic tone, about a good-looking person acting in line with, or relying on, their looks. It is not a safe compliment, so use other words when you simply want to praise someone's appearance.

examples.en: The market is so noisy that I have to raise my voice.
On holidays the house is lively and noisy.
We ate dinner in a boisterous atmosphere.

examples.ko: 옆 테이블이 너무 왁자지껄해서 이야기하기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The next table was so loud that it was hard to talk.
The noisy classroom went quiet when the teacher walked in.
The classroom is so noisy, so I'll close the window.

explain: '왁자지껄한 분위기', '왁자지껄하던 교실'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미거나 '~이 왁자지껄하다'로 써요. 반대말은 '조용하다'예요. 사람들이 많이 모여 시끄러운 장면에 써요.
explain_en: It can modify a noun, as in '왁자지껄한 분위기' and '왁자지껄하던 교실', or be used as '~이 왁자지껄하다'. Its opposite is '조용하다'. It is used for scenes where many people have gathered and it is loud.
